task: Mass-delete legacy posts before autonomous posting cron starts
method: Chrome MCP web UI deletion (Meta Graph IG content_publish blocked pending business verification)
notes: All 59 deletions executed via the same UI flow: click first post tile -> click kebab (top-right of modal) -> click Delete -> confirm Delete in modal.

Layout coordinates shifted twice during the run as the post grid shrank. Initial layout: tile (316,585), kebab (1313,47). Below ~12 posts: tile (386,710), kebab (1297,47). Confirm-dialog Delete button stayed at (777,283) regardless.
No 'we've limited your activity', 'try again later', or action-blocked warnings appeared at any point. Account remained healthy throughout.
Header post-count is cached on the profile page and only updates after a fresh navigation. Verified counts via: 59 -> 11 -> 10 -> 5 -> 1 -> 0 by hard-refreshing.

Post URLs were captured from the discovery scan and during deletions; the full per-post log is not exhaustive (logging every shortcode mid-loop would have doubled run time). The deletion-count delta is the source of truth: 59 -> 0.

recommendations.whenToStartPosting: Wait 24h before resuming autonomous posting. IG sometimes flags accounts that go from 0 -> high-frequency posting immediately after a mass delete. Soft start: 1-2 manual-quality posts within 24h, then let cron resume daily 10am AEST.
recommendations.rateLimitObserved: None during deletion. If cron's first post fails with action_blocked, pause 48h before retry.
recommendations.businessVerification: Still pending; once cleared (~2026-05-07/08), instagram_content_publish unblocks API posting. Direct-API posts are less likely to trigger flags than browser automation.
